title: model-loading-weights-shard-debug-scratchpad-danielle-park
content:
Context:
- Repro of customer incident: partial weights download during model start causes process to fail after ~30s when trying to map shards to disk. Customer on Dedicated; using model: gptx-13b-quant-sharded, shard count 8, S3-backed checkpoint with pre-signed URLs via internal proxy.

What happened (observed):
- Runtime logs show repeated 403s for a subset of shard URLs at startup (see errors below).
- Download threads eventually time out, we trigger model unload/rollback and fallback to smaller model.
- File system shows incomplete .part files for 2 shards; size mismatch vs manifest.

Commands I ran locally to reproduce:
- curl -I <presigned-url-for-shard-3> -> 403 intermittently
- aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-model-bucket --key checkpoints/gptx-13b/shard-3 -> success from my laptop creds
- wget --tries=1 --timeout=10 -O /tmp/shard-3.part "<presigned-url>" -> HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden (repeatable from our test infra)
- ./run_local_runtime --model-dir /tmp/gptx-13b-checkpoint --shards-manifest manifest.json --log-level debug

Error snippets (from runtime logs):
- [2026-02-15T14:12:03Z] ERROR shard-downloader: failed to fetch shard 3 url="<redacted>" status=403 code=Forbidden msg="Pre-signed URL expired or invalid signature"
- [2026-02-15T14:12:03Z] WARN shard-manager: incomplete shard file detected shard=3 size=0 expected=512MB
- [2026-02-15T14:12:35Z] ERROR model-loader: model gptx-13b-quant-sharded failed to load: incomplete checkpoint (2/8 shards missing)

Hypotheses:
1) Presigned URLs are being generated with too-short TTL or wrong signing key when proxying through token-exchange service (most likely).
2) Network path from Dedicated nodes to S3 occasionally hits a corporate proxy that strips Authorization header for large files -> results in 403.
3) Our shard manifest has stale checksums causing downloader to retry wrong URLs (less likely given 403).
4) Concurrency limit on proxy causes 429/403 fallback in some cases; retry logic not exponential enough.

What I tried so far (quick fixes):
- Extended presigned URL TTL in a local test generator to 1 hour -> wget succeeded consistently.
- Added additional retries with backoff in the downloader (patched locally) -> reduces but does not eliminate failures when 403 is immediate.
- Forced downloads to go through a direct S3 signed URL (bypassing proxy) in a staging Dedicated node -> worked.

Open questions / next steps:
- Does the token-exchange/proxy rotate signing keys per-request? Need to confirm with infra. (Pinged @Jordan Wu in Slack)
- Add counters in the proxy for Authorization header presence/absence and response codes for model shard requests.
- Improve runtime to validate ETag/size streaming while downloading and fail earlier with clearer message.
- For now, implement a defensive fallback: if >1 shard 403 on initial attempt, fall back to fetching direct S3 signed URL (if customer config allows).
- Create a small integration test: simulate proxy that randomly strips Authorization and assert downloader handles or reports cleanly.

Notes to self:
- Keep repro script in /home/dpark/tmp/shard-repro/ and add to ticket.
- Check with infra: when Dedicated nodes use NAT/proxy, do they reuse connections or rotate? Could be related to signature/mismatch window.
- Follow up on PR 1890 (adds retry/backoff) to see if we need more conservative behavior for shard downloads.

Attachments / artifacts to copy into ticket:
- /home/dpark/logs/gptx-13b-20260215-debug.log (contains 403 tracebacks)
- minimal repro script: users/danielle-park/shard-download-repro.sh

Immediate TODOs (next 48h):
- [ ] Confirm presigned URL TTL behavior with token-exchange (owner: Jordan)
- [ ] Add proxy metrics for auth header and response codes (owner: Liam)
- [ ] Land a defensive fallback in runtime to request direct signed URL if allowed (owner: Danielle)
- [ ] Add integration test to CI that simulates header-stripping proxy (owner: Danielle/Maya)

End of scratchpad.
